finding.title: Cross-Sender idempotencyKey Collision in ChatController Overwrites Messages and Spoofs E2EE Sender Attribution
finding.description: The backend and PostgreSQL restrict idempotency_key uniqueness solely per sender: CONSTRAINT messages_idempotency_uq UNIQUE (sender_id, idempotency_key) in sql/index.sql:68. However, ChatController.#entries in the browser indexes all room messages solely by message.idempotencyKey (without senderId). Furthermore, when #decrypt(message) returns null, ChatController.#receive reuses any plaintext previously stored under that same key: entries.set(key, toEntry(message, text ?? entries.get(key)?.text ?? null)). Because any room member observes idempotencyKey values in message.new frames or REST history, a malicious room member (Bob) can reuse another member's (Alice's) idempotencyKey to: (1) overwrite Alice's message in other members' chat views, and (2) spoof E2EE sender attribution when an undecryptable message from Alice (e.g. from an earlier keyEpoch) is re-evaluated on sender-keys.available and inherits Bob's decrypted plaintext.
finding.root_cause: ChatController.#entries (src/frontend/messaging/application/chat.controller.ts:135) uses only message.idempotencyKey as the Map key, and ChatController.#receive (line 843) falls back to entries.get(key)?.text without verifying that the existing entry belongs to the same senderId or message.id.

trace.step: Receives message.new and sender-keys.available WebSocket frames with MessageView payloads exposing idempotencyKey.
Forwards incoming MessageView records to this.#receive(message).
On sender-keys.available, re-invokes #receive(message) for undecrypted messages in #undecrypted matching (roomId, keyEpoch).
Executes entries.set(key, toEntry(message, text ?? entries.get(key)?.text ?? null)) using key = message.idempotencyKey.

reproduction.observed_result: 1. Alice's epoch-1 message initially renders as "Unable to decrypt" (undecryptable: true). 2. Bob sends an epoch-2 message with the same idempotencyKey and plaintext "FORGED BY BOB: Wire funds to account 999". 3. On sender-keys.available, #receive(aliceMessage) fails decryption (null), reads entries.get(key)?.text, and renders "FORGED BY BOB: Wire funds to account 999" under sender: "User 1" (Alice) with undecryptable: false.

finding.remediation: Key #entries by `${message.senderId}:${message.idempotencyKey}` (or message.id) and only preserve existing.text when existing.senderId === message.senderId and (existing.id === null || existing.id === message.id).

lead.title: CI workflow executes pull_request code without narrowing GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
lead.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on push (main) and pull_request, checks out PR code via actions/checkout@v4 (default persist-credentials: true), and executes repository code (bun fmt, bun lint, typecheck, tests) without declaring a read-only permissions: block.
lead.claimed_root_cause: Missing permissions: { contents: read } and persist-credentials: false in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

blockers.blocker: GitHub Actions default Workflow permissions setting (read-only vs read-write) is not visible in source.
Branch protection rules on main are not visible in source.

lead.validation_plan: Check GitHub Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN default scope; add top-level permissions: { contents: read } and persist-credentials: false on actions/checkout@v4.

lead.title: Podman pod publishes unauthenticated Valkey and default-credential PostgreSQL ports without loopback host binding
lead.description: scripts/pod.ts publishes ports 3001:3000, 5433:5432, and 6380:6379 without a 127.0.0.1: prefix, binding 0.0.0.0 by default. Valkey runs without requirepass (and protected-mode no in the image) and Postgres runs with static chat:chat credentials. On an untrusted network without a host firewall, peers could flush revoked-session:<sid> or rl:* keys in Valkey or access Postgres.
lead.claimed_root_cause: scripts/pod.ts:44 omits 127.0.0.1: in -p and starts Valkey without auth and Postgres with chat:chat.

blockers.blocker: Actual host network exposure and firewall rules (nftables/ufw) when running the pod.

lead.validation_plan: Run `ss -tlnp '( sport = :5433 or sport = :6380 )'` and inspect host firewall while pod is running; prefix `-p 127.0.0.1:` in scripts/pod.ts:44 for Postgres and Valkey.

lead.title: Auth endpoints parse JSON bodies via uncapped request.json() instead of readCappedText
lead.description: POST /api/auth/sign-in and POST /api/auth/sign-up use request.json() in readCredentials instead of readCappedText(request, MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES) (64 KiB) used by readJsonObject in messaging, and createServer omits maxRequestBodySize on Bun.serve (default 128 MiB).
lead.claimed_root_cause: src/backend/user/presentation/user.controller.ts:79 calls request.json() without a byte-length cap.

blockers.blocker: Deployed ingress/proxy body size limits (Cloudflare/nginx) outside the repository.

lead.validation_plan: Send a >64 KiB POST to /api/auth/sign-in against createServer locally and check production ingress limits.
